title: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense
line: Black attacks White's center pawn instead of copying the bishop, and gives a pawn for quick play.

steps.text: Black brings out the other knight instead of the bishop. It attacks your pawn on e4.
Jump the knight forward. With the bishop it attacks f7, which only the king guards.

also.d2d3: Guarding the pawn is the quiet main line. This lesson goes for f7.

steps.after: Black blocks the bishop with a pawn.

steps.text: Take the pawn. It blocked your bishop, and now the pawn on d5 is yours.
steps.after: Black does not take back. The knight attacks your bishop instead.

steps.text: If the knight took back on d5, your knight could take on f7: the next lesson. So Black gives up a pawn and chases the bishop.
Move the bishop away with check, so Black must answer the check first.
steps.after: Black blocks with a pawn and offers it.

steps.text: Take the pawn. You are a pawn ahead, and it would have chased your bishop.
Your bishop is attacked again. Bring it back home to safety.

also.b5d3: That square is also played. This lesson goes back to e2.
also.d1f3: The queen move is also played. This lesson moves the bishop back.

steps.text: The pawn attacks your knight. Step it back to f3, where it guards the center.

also.g5h3: That square is also played. This lesson goes back to f3.

steps.text: The pawn chases the knight once more. Jump into the center.
steps.after: You are a pawn up, but Black has quick play while your pieces were pushed back. That is the price of the early attack.

summary: Black meets the attack on its weak pawn by giving a pawn back, and gains time chasing White's pieces.
